H — Analysis / use: VICTRE-shaped validation + black-box target

Letter folder H_analysis/ of the Quantum Phantoms reverse-engineering epic (epic). Markdown is the source of truth; python -m shared.site.build renders it to site/H_analysis/index.html. Target states live only in status.json (lifecycle: listed → dissected → reproduced → adapted → integrated | rejected).

Purpose

VICTRE-modelled study architecture over the hybrid volumes: physics realism (HU, edge, NPS vs LIDC), PyRadiomics distributions, in-context visual Turing test, train-synthetic/test-real detection, cohort drift vs rulebook, certificate and witness statistics, classical baseline. AI-Rad Companion only as a documented-interface black box (no decompiling).

How to run (sim commands)

Working directory reverse-engineering/. Environment: base Python 3.13 works (radiomics-lite engine); requirements.txt documents the qp-re-h env for PyRadiomics.

python -m H_analysis.repro.r20a_cho_ideal                       # CHO vs analytic ideal observer (~3 min)
python -m H_analysis.repro.r20b_victre_design                   # VICTRE design -> SE(dAUC) (~25 min)
python -m H_analysis.src.lidc_ref --scans all                   # real-nodule reference (LIDC on disk, ~30 min)
python -m H_analysis.src.report --cohort H_analysis/cohorts/stub.json --lidc-ref none      # stub smoke test
python -m H_analysis.src.pilot plan --hosts 20 --per-host 3     # then: bash H_analysis/runs/<ts>-pilot/commands.sh
python -m H_analysis.src.report --cohort H_analysis/runs/<ts>-pilot/cohort.json --lidc-ref H_analysis/runs/<ts>-lidc-ref
python -m H_analysis.src.turing_kit --manifest <cohort.json> --lidc-ref <run> --n 40
python -m H_analysis.src.turing_score answers.json key.json
python -m H_analysis.src.airad_check <dicom_dir>

Every quantum number in a report keeps its label ("simulated: ideal" / "simulated: Heron-class noise (FakeMarrakesh)"); no hardware numbers exist.

Cohort manifest format

cohorts/*.json, paths relative to the manifest, every file checked with shared.validate (a failure aborts the report, nothing is written): seed_note, hybrids[]{path, seed_source?: certified|prng}, draws[], rulebook, compiled_circuit, job_records[], certificates[], witness[], memory[], simulability[], trajectories[], receipts[], ledger. seed_source lives in the manifest because the contracts have no field for it.

Outputs: ValidationReport section layout (de-facto sub-schema, CCR-H1)

realism            {per_type:{type:{metric:{syn[], real_summary{p5,p50,p95,n}, syn_percentile[], ks_D, ks_p, pass}}}, shell_noise_ratio, n}
radiomics          {engine:"radiomics-lite", n_features, frac_abs_smd_lt_0p5, c2st{auc,ci95}, null{frac_abs_smd_lt_0p5,c2st_auc}, per_feature_ref}
utility            {task, observer:"CHO-LG3D", n_readers, n_train, n_test{pos,neg}, auc_train_syn, auc_train_real, delta_auc{value,se,ci95,df}, per_type, auc_2d_central_slice, powered}
drift              {by_sim_label:{label:{per_node:{tvd,rmspe_pct,chi2_p,n}, joint_tvd, invalid_shot_fraction, n}}, cohort, exact_marginals}
certificate_stats  {certificates{by_sim_label}, witnesses, memory, simulability, bp_simulability_join, receipts, hardware:null, certification_status}
baseline           {pairs[]{quantity, quantum_value, classical_value, note, sim_label}, seed_source_arm, honesty{ok,...}}

Sections without inputs read {"status": "insufficient input", "n": ...}. report_detail.json (per-lesion / per-feature tables) sits beside the report and is not part of the contract.

Pipeline readiness

Prototype

Draft rating, not yet confirmed by the chain (the chain has not reached H). H's CLI accepts the chain's cohort manifest (the runner writes it in H's format), but the analysis is n = 1 in INT: MRMC and train-synthetic/test-real sections cannot give a number, and H does not yet label them "n=1 — not powered". R20b is not matched (SE 0.0033–0.0051 vs 0.0073), the pilot never ran, and radiomics is the lite engine. No lidc_ref run is on disk, so the first chain also pays a full LIDC reference pass.

Weak links

Weak link Kind Why it limits reliability Evidence To strengthen

R20b not matched component the MRMC variance model is too homogeneous R20b row heterogeneous surrogate

No cached LIDC reference precondition the first validate stage runs a full lidc_ref H_analysis/runs/ absent run lidc_ref once; the runner reuses the latest

Used as-is in the chain? Expected yes; its numbers will be n = 1 and must be read as plumbing, not validation. Full gap list: INT; whole chain: index.

Future

Shared, pipeline-wide context (end goal, digital-twin path, cross-letter risks) lives once in the whole-pipeline Future. This section covers only what this letter adds. Every claim carries a label: evidence-based (a number in this repo or a cited paper), extrapolation (a reasoned step beyond the evidence), speculative (possible, not supported yet).

1. Aim of the paper(s)

  • [H03] Badano et al. (VICTRE): an entirely in-silico imaging trial that reproduced the conclusion of a real clinical trial, and a precedent for regulatory use of simulation.
  • [H04] Abadi, [G03] Badano, [G02] AAPM TG-387: virtual clinical trials, stochastic digital human cohorts, and their role in regulatory science.
  • [F10] Chuquicusma: a visual Turing test (can radiologists tell synthetic nodules from real ones?). [H01] train-synthetic/test-real detection. [H05] PyRadiomics features.
  • #21 AI-Rad Companion: a commercial chest-CT assistant, treated as a documented-interface black box.

Why it matters: the whole pipeline is only worth something if real-world evidence shows synthetic cohorts change detector performance on real patients.

2. Contribution

  • A channelized Hotelling observer checked against the analytic ideal observer (max difference 0.0054). evidence-based
  • MRMC variance reproduction not matched (SE 0.0033–0.0051 vs 0.0073). evidence-based
  • A six-section validation report (realism, radiomics, utility, drift, certificate statistics, baseline), plus a cohort manifest that INT writes from real chain files. evidence-based
  • A longitudinal protocol for AI-Rad Companion: reported vs true volume and doubling time (not run). evidence-based

3. Role in cancer detection

End goal: show, with powered statistics, that (a) readers cannot tell synthetic from real nodules, (b) detectors trained or tested on synthetic cohorts behave the same on real data, and (c) a commercial assistant's volume and growth errors can be measured against exact ground truth. This is the evidence a clinical partner needs. extrapolation

4. Beyond lungs

  • Virtual trials for any device or AI [H04, G02]: the VICTRE design is not lung-specific. evidence-based
  • In-silico arms for treatment studies. Once E/F model response, H's design could compare virtual cohorts under different therapies. speculative

5. Long-term vision: toward a digital twin

speculative A twin is only as trustworthy as its validation framework. Path: (1) one-tumour report (INT, n = 1) → (2) pilot cohorts (20 hosts × 3 placement classes) → (3) reader studies and train-synthetic/test-real at power → (4) continuous validation of each twin's forecasts against that patient's next real scan.

6. Predictions

5 years Assumptions: public LIDC data; radiomics-lite (no new installs); small reader pools.

  • Every section can be produced, but n = 1 gives no powered statistic. evidence-based
  • A pilot cohort with a visual Turing test and a train-synthetic/test-real detection experiment. extrapolation

10 years Assumptions: access to multi-centre data and reader panels; accepted virtual-trial methodology [G02].

  • In-silico validation of a nodule-detection product, in the style of VICTRE, as supporting evidence. extrapolation

15 years Assumptions: fault-tolerant hardware; mature twin cohorts.

  • speculative Analysis stays classical. Quantum machine-learning detectors may be benchmarked here against classical ones under fair rules [H06, H09], but a practical advantage on imaging data is unproven.
